name: Rijksmuseum
description: The Netherlands’ national museum, in a grand 1885 building: Rembrandt’s The Night Watch, Vermeer and Dutch Golden Age art.

name: Amsterdam Centraal
description: The city’s main railway station, a brick palace of a building on the waterfront that opened in 1889.

name: Dam Square
description: The city’s main square, with the Royal Palace, the Nieuwe Kerk and the white National Monument to the Second World War.

name: Van Gogh Museum
description: The world’s largest collection of Van Gogh’s paintings, drawings and letters, on Museumplein.

name: Oude Kerk
description: Amsterdam’s oldest building, a medieval church in the middle of the red-light district, now also used for contemporary art.

name: Waag
description: A 15th-century city gate later used as a weigh house, standing in the middle of Nieuwmarkt square. It is now a restaurant.

name: Anne Frank House
description: The canal house where Anne Frank and her family hid from the Nazis for two years. The secret annexe is now a museum.

name: Flower Market
description: A flower market on a row of floating stalls along the Singel canal, selling bulbs, plants and cut flowers.

name: East India House
description: The 17th-century headquarters of the Dutch East India Company (VOC), now part of the University of Amsterdam.

name: Vondelpark
description: The city’s best-known park, opened in 1865 just south of the centre, with ponds, lawns and cycle paths.

name: Dutch Resistance Museum
description: A museum about the Dutch Resistance and daily life in Amsterdam under German occupation in the Second World War.

name: Leidseplein
description: A busy square on the edge of the canal ring, lined with theatres, bars and music venues.

name: De Hallen
description: A former tram depot from the early 1900s, converted into a food hall, a cinema and denim workshops.
